premise: Stepping away from a secure government job to autonomously supply battlefields during the American Civil War.
hook: A quiet government clerk packed her own wagons with medical supplies and rode directly onto active civil war battlefields.
key_facts: Worked as one of the first female clerks in the US Patent Office.
Resigned her post in 1861 to independently distribute food and bandages to soldiers.
Gained permission from Union commanders to travel with army ambulances.
Later founded the American Red Cross in 1881.

premise: Rising from the slums of Bauru to win the World Cup at just 17 years old.
hook: He played barefoot with socks stuffed with rags because his family could not afford a real leather football.
key_facts: Born Edson Arantes do Nascimento in poverty in Minas Gerais, Brazil.
Learned to play soccer using grapefruits and rolled-up rags in the streets.
Made his international debut for Brazil at age 16.
Scored two goals in the 1958 World Cup final to secure Brazil's first title.

premise: Refusing to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, sparking a pivotal movement against racial segregation.
hook: Her decision on a crowded city bus was a deliberate, courageous stand built on years of civil rights activism.
key_facts: Worked as a seamstress and served as secretary for the Montgomery chapter of the NAACP.
Was arrested on December 1, 1955, for violating Montgomery's segregation ordinances.
Triggered the 381-day Montgomery bus boycott organized by local Black leaders.
The boycott led to a U.S. Supreme Court ruling declaring segregated buses unconstitutional.

premise: Choosing not to patent the polio vaccine, making it freely available to the public during a terrifying global epidemic.
hook: When asked who owned the patent to the polio vaccine that saved millions of children, he simply replied: 'The people, I would say. There is no patent.'
key_facts: Led the research team that developed one of the first successful polio vaccines in the early 1950s.
Polio epidemics regularly paralyzed or killed thousands of children annually prior to the vaccine.
The decision to forgo patenting meant losing billions of potential personal dollars for the greater public good.
Archival newsreels and press conferences capture the massive public relief following the vaccine trials.
